22 CLASSICS / 16 WINNERS
There have been 22 Rex Mays Classics run at the Wiscon-
sin State Fair Speedway. A total of 16 different drivers were
first under the checkered flag. That means some had to take
more than one victory.
The first of the multi-race winners was the late Tony Bet-
tenhausen. He copped the first two editions in 1950 and 1951.
Johnny Thompson of Boyertown, Pa., picked off the 1955 event
and repeated in 1959. Meanwhile, Rodger Ward won his first
Classic in 1957. Ward went on to become the winnest driver in
the Mays series, taking the 1960, 1961 and 1963 races. A. J.
A
Foyt was the last double victor with checkereds in 1962 and 1964.
The other dozen events went to 12 drivers, Mike Nazaruk
(1952), Jack McGrath (1953), Chuck Stevenson (1954), Pat
Flaherty (1956), Art Bisch (1958), Parnelli Jones (1965), Mario
Andretti (1966), Gordon Johncock (1967), Lloyd Ruby (1968),
Art Pollard (1969), Joe Leonard (1970) and Al Unser (1971).
AN UNPRECEDENTED fourth victory in the Rex Mays Classic had
just been recorded by Rodger Ward, following the 1963 event.

On a race track such as the Wis-

consin State Fair Speedway every
LARI
driver who enters gets an equal chance.
His race car takes up the same amount
of space on the racing surface, regard-
less of his previous accomplishments,
or lack of them.
In today's race seasoned drivers
who can count their experience in
decades and rookies who are mainly
backed by lots of hope and courage,
will take to the oval.
' The outcome is not guaranteed. On
this page are three drivers, two that
have been around a long time and one
that hasn't. All will have to give their
best — or be left behind. That is the
stuff auto racing is made of.
ROGER McCLUSKEY, 41 of Tucson, Ariz., has been racing since 1949 when he started in stocks.
He has had great success in sprint cars and late models, but in more than 10 years of Champion-
ship racing has not done as well. He won the USAC sprint title in 1963 and 1966 and the
stock crown in 1969 and 1970. Finishing 13th in Championship points last year, Roger has two
wins to his credit in his career. His rough championship luck was evident in last year's Rex
Mays Classic when he finished 23rd out of 24 starters, thanks to throttle trouble. He drives a
radical new Manta this year.
Wayne Doebling Photo
A. J. FOYT finished second on the Cham-
pionship Trail last year and his Coyote
III-Ford carries the number two, but in all
areas of USAC Championship racing he is
number one. His accomplishments in racing
would fill this entire program. Briefly he is
the all-time point leader, has won the most
races (43), won the most Championship titles
(five) and has taken the prestiegous In-
dianapolis 500 three times. A. J. Foyt is
probably the greatest automobile racing
driver of all times.
Wayne Doebling Photo
MIKE HISS is a rookie. This is his first year
as a Championship Trail driver. Unless you
are a Mark Donohue, being a rookie is a
rough road — at best. Hiss raced in the
Sports Car Club of America Continental
Formula B series and finished seventh last
year, up two places from his ninth place
finish of 1970. The move from a relatively
low-powered Formula B car on a road
course to the powerful Championship cars
on an oval is a big step. So far the Tustin,
Calif. driver is doing well.
